correctness.rationale: On probability Haar torus, the fourth power is exactly the additive energy sum_h r(h)^2. If h has positive and negative coordinate totals P and Q, then lattice simplex intersection counts are r(h)=binom(n-max(P,Q)+d,d) when max(P,Q)<=n. For each sign-pattern with p positive and q negative coordinates, positive compositions with sum<=t and negative compositions contribute binom(t,p)binom(t,q); summing multinomial choices counts A_d(t). The exact shell difference supplies the finite formula. Direct independent pair-difference energy enumeration and the binomial formula agree for (d,n)=(2,2):102,(2,4):1443,(3,3):2364,(4,2):835. The degree-d leading coefficient of A_d is binom(2d,d)/d! by Vandermonde; beta integration and the simplex lattice count yield the stated factorial constants. Stirling gives the precise (16/27)^d rate; box product correlation gives (2/3)^d. Limits are iterated n->infinity at fixed d, then d->infinity, not simultaneous uniformity.

value.rationale: The all-dimensional exact additive energy of a standard simplex is a natural Fourier invariant, with a sharp dimension-dependent normalized contrast to a box; the finite formula and factorial profile go substantially beyond the previously known six-character special case and order-of-growth estimates. Such an exact object/invariant pair can serve as a baseline for Fourier truncation and additive combinatorics without needing a downstream theorem.

limitations: Standard unit-coefficient lattice simplex and probability Haar normalization only.
No weighted Fourier coefficients or arbitrary rational polytope.
